evals.prompt: I'm setting up ANC indicators on a 2.41 instance that was built from the Sierra Leone demo. I need two aggregate indicators: (1) ANC 1-3 dropout rate, as a percentage of women who came for ANC 1st visit but not a 3rd, and (2) % of ANC 1st visits done at outreach (vs fixed). Our metadata extract is in evals/files/sl-anc-extract.json, including my draft of the dropout rate. The district managers want the district figure to be the average of the facility rates. Can you fix my draft, write both indicators as JSON I can POST to /api/indicators (save it as indicators.json), and tell me anything else I should check before I trust the numbers?
evals.expected_output: indicators.json with two indicators on the Percent (factor 100) type ItPercent01: dropout numerator #{fbfJHSPpUQD} - #{Jtf34kNZhzP}, denominator #{fbfJHSPpUQD}, no *100 in the expression; outreach numerator #{fbfJHSPpUQD.pq2XI5kz2BY}, denominator #{fbfJHSPpUQD} (or Fixed + Outreach COCs; any extra indicators flagged as optional). Explains the draft is 100x too large (factor + *100) and that the inner division aborts the whole analytics request with 409 E7132 where ANC 1st visit is 0, whereas a zero denominator field just yields no value for that cell; flags ANC 3rd visit aggregationType AVERAGE (should be SUM); explains parent values are sum(num)/sum(den), not an average of facility rates, and either keeps the pooled rate or also offers a correctly guarded subExpression() facility average with the trade-off flagged (both acceptable; claiming the average is impossible is not); asks about or flags a naming convention; recommends validating each expression with GET /api/expressions/description.
assertions: indicators.json is valid JSON and contains the two requested indicators (the ANC 1-3 dropout rate and the % of ANC 1st visits at outreach), each with numerator, denominator and indicatorType fields. Extra indicator objects (e.g. pooled and facility-average variants) are allowed if the answer labels which is which and flags any extras as optional/additional
Both indicators reference indicator type ItPercent01 (factor 100), and neither numerator nor denominator contains a '* 100' or '*100' multiplier

The dropout rate moves the division out of a plain numerator. Accept either (a) the pooled form: numerator #{fbfJHSPpUQD} - #{Jtf34kNZhzP}, denominator #{fbfJHSPpUQD}; or (b) a facility-average form built with subExpression(...) that computes the per-facility rate with a guard against ANC 1st visit = 0 and aggregates it correctly (e.g. denominator counting facilities with ANC1 > 0, or .aggregationType(AVERAGE)). If (b) is the main deliverable, the pooled form (a) must also be supplied, in indicators.json or a clearly labelled companion file, and the answer must flag the weighting trade-off. The draft's (ANC1 - ANC3)/ANC1 inside a plain numerator with denominator 1 fails

The outreach indicator counts the Outreach category option combo #{fbfJHSPpUQD.pq2XI5kz2BY}: as the plain numerator (pooled form) or inside a per-facility subExpression ratio (facility-average form). A filter/condition on a category option, or the whole #{fbfJHSPpUQD}, as the outreach count fails

The outreach share is taken over all ANC 1st visits: in the pooled form the denominator is #{fbfJHSPpUQD} or #{fbfJHSPpUQD.PT59n8BQbqM} + #{fbfJHSPpUQD.pq2XI5kz2BY} (Fixed + Outreach); in a facility-average form the per-facility ratio divides by the same total. Dividing by a single COC (e.g. Fixed only, which gives an outreach:fixed ratio) fails
States that the draft is inflated because the Percent type already multiplies by 100 (so the draft is 100x too big)

States both halves of the contrast: a division inside the numerator ((#{fbfJHSPpUQD} - #{Jtf34kNZhzP}) / #{fbfJHSPpUQD}) makes the whole analytics request fail (HTTP 409 / E7132, division by zero) as soon as any requested org unit/period has ANC 1st visit = 0, whereas a zero in the indicator's denominator field only leaves that one cell without a value. Mentioning E7132 or the abort without the zero-denominator contrast fails
Flags that ANC 3rd visit (Jtf34kNZhzP) has aggregationType AVERAGE in the extract and should be SUM, and that the expression review alone would not catch this

Tells the user that a standard indicator yields sum of numerators / sum of denominators at district level (a weighted rate), not the average of facility percentages. If it builds a facility-average (subExpression, predictors, AVERAGE-aggregated outputs), it flags the weighting trade-off; it must not claim the average is impossible in an aggregate indicator on 2.41 (subExpression() makes it possible)

If the answer describes a workaround for the average-of-facility-rates request (subExpression(), predictors, AVERAGE-aggregated output data elements), any limitation it attributes to that workaround is factually correct. In particular it does not claim subExpression() may reference only one data element (subExpression(#{A}/#{B}) with several data elements/operands is valid). Passes if no workaround is described
evals.notes: Aggregate authoring traps: double factor, inner division E7132, COC enumeration, DE aggregationType lint, parent recombination; expressions checkable live via GET /api/expressions/description on any SL demo.

evals.prompt: We're on 2.42.3 with the Sierra Leone demo Child Programme. We added a multi-select data element 'CH Postnatal danger signs' to the Baby Postnatal stage (see evals/files/child-programme-danger-signs.json). I need program indicators for (a) number of postnatal visits per month where convulsions (DS1) were recorded, (b) number of postnatal visits per month with skin pustules (DS10), and (c) number of children with any danger sign recorded at a postnatal visit, per quarter. I tried the filter d2:containsItems(#{ZzYYXq4fJie.PnDangrSg01}, 'DS1') in Maintenance and it says 'Expression is not valid' / 'Invalid string token d', so I guess PIs can't handle multi-select. My colleague suggests a program rule that assigns 12 yes/no data elements instead. Should we do that? If not, give me the PIs as JSON for POST /api/programIndicators (save as program-indicators.json).
evals.expected_output: Advises against the 12 flag data elements: containsItems() exists in PIs on 2.41+ but without the d2: prefix (d2: is the program-rule form). program-indicators.json has (a) and (b) as EVENT/COUNT PIs with filters V{program_stage_id} == 'ZzYYXq4fJie' && containsItems(#{ZzYYXq4fJie.PnDangrSg01}, 'DS1' / 'DS10'); warns that contains() would make 'DS1' match 'DS10'; (c) counts children, not visits: ENROLLMENT type with a d2:hasValue-style filter and a caveat to probe that the event DE resolves in ENROLLMENT type, or EVENT type with V{tei_count}; either way a child is placed in the quarter of a danger-sign visit (EVENT_DATE boundaries, not PS_EVENTDATE-only, which leaves d2:count/#{stage.de} lookups unbounded in 2.42); every PI carries explicit analyticsPeriodBoundaries (API-created PIs are otherwise unbounded), with (c) bounded on the event date (EVENT_DATE) rather than enrollment date; validate with POST /api/programIndicators/filter/description (text/plain).
assertions: Says containsItems is available in program indicators and the error comes from the d2: prefix: indicators/PIs use the unprefixed containsItems(), the d2: form belongs to program rules
Recommends against the 12 rule-assigned yes/no data elements
program-indicators.json is valid JSON and every filter that tests an option uses 'containsItems(' with no 'd2:containsItems' anywhere in the file
Warns that contains() is a substring match that would count 'DS10' (and 'DS11', 'DS12') as DS1, so containsItems is required here
PIs (a) and (b) use analyticsType EVENT with aggregationType COUNT (or SUM of 1) and keep the option test in the filter rather than a d2:condition in the expression

PI (c) counts each child once per quarter, not once per visit: either analyticsType ENROLLMENT, or analyticsType EVENT with expression V{tei_count} (distinct tracked entities). A plain EVENT/COUNT PI (V{event_count} or 1) for (c) fails, and the answer explains that the stage is repeatable so visit-level counting would count a child several times

PI (c) places each child in the quarter of a danger-sign visit: a child with a Baby Postnatal visit in the quarter but a danger sign recorded only at a visit outside the quarter is NOT counted. Acceptable: EVENT type with EVENT_DATE boundaries and the danger-sign test in the filter; or ENROLLMENT type whose danger-sign lookup (#{ZzYYXq4fJie.PnDangrSg01} / d2:hasValue / d2:count...) is bounded by EVENT_DATE boundaries. Fails: ENROLLMENT with only PS_EVENTDATE:ZzYYXq4fJie (or enrollment-date) boundaries around a d2:count/#{stage.de} danger-sign test, because in 2.42 those stage-data lookups honour only EVENT_DATE boundaries, so the test sees danger signs from any date
Every PI in program-indicators.json has a non-empty analyticsPeriodBoundaries array, and the answer says a PI POSTed via the API without boundaries is unbounded (same all-time value for every period)

Gives the exact validation call for the filters: POST /api/programIndicators/filter/description with the raw filter string as a text/plain body (a JSON {"expression": ...} body with Content-Type application/json is equally valid; for expressions, POST /api/programIndicators/expression/description). 'Paste it into Maintenance' or a GET call alone does not pass
evals.notes: MULTI_TEXT trap (d2: prefix error read as 'unsupported'), contains vs containsItems substring, EVENT vs ENROLLMENT, API boundary omission; filters checkable live via /api/programIndicators/filter/description once the DE is imported.

evals.prompt: This rate looks wrong and I can't see why. On our Sierra Leone demo copy (2.42) I scripted a small Child Programme dashboard: postnatal visits, low birth weight births, postnatal visits for LBW babies, and an aggregate % indicator on top. The export and what analytics returns for Sierra Leone Jan-Mar 2024 are in evals/files/lbw-dashboard-export.json. Postnatal visits is 1.0 every month, LBW births is 1284 in every single month, and the % is always 0. Yesterday I changed something on the postnatal visits PI through the API and the chart still shows exactly the same numbers, so I don't think that was it. Is it the Percent indicator type? What's broken and how do I fix and prove it?
evals.expected_output: Four separate root causes: PiPncVisit1 uses aggregationType AVERAGE on V{event_count} (returns ~1; must be COUNT/SUM); PiLbwBirth1 has no analyticsPeriodBoundaries because it was created via the API, so it is unbounded and returns the same all-time value for every period (add the EVENT_DATE start/end boundaries); PiPncLbw001 is an EVENT PI anchored on Baby Postnatal events but reads a Birth-stage DE, which is null on those rows, so it is always 0 (anchor on the Birth stage, or ENROLLMENT with a probe to confirm it resolves), with boundaries that still find a birth in an earlier month than the PNC visit, and a % whose numerator and denominator have the same unit (babies/babies or visits/visits); the unchanged chart after the fix is analytics caching / not clearing the cache or re-running analytics, not proof that the change was irrelevant. The Percent type (factor 100) is correct. Proof: cacheClear or _cb, re-run analytics, throwaway probe PIs or line-level events query, period-edge test.
assertions: Identifies that PiPncVisit1 combines a count-style expression (V{event_count}) with aggregationType AVERAGE, which yields ~1, and says to change it to COUNT (or SUM)

Identifies that PiLbwBirth1 has no analyticsPeriodBoundaries and that an API-created PI without boundaries is unbounded, which explains the identical 1284 in every month; supplies the EVENT_DATE AFTER_START/BEFORE_END boundaries as the fix

Identifies that PiPncLbw001 is an EVENT-type PI on Baby Postnatal events reading a Birth-stage data element (#{A03MvHHogjR.UXz7xuGCEhU}), which is null on those rows, so the filter never matches even though the expression validates

Gives a concrete fix for the cross-stage PI (anchor on the Birth stage, or switch to ENROLLMENT) and, if ENROLLMENT is proposed, says to confirm with a probe that the event data element resolves in enrollment analytics

The fixed % indicator has matching units in numerator and denominator (LBW babies / babies, or visits for LBW babies / postnatal visits) and the answer says which one it is. A numerator counting babies/enrollments over PiPncVisit1 counting visits (or the reverse) fails

The cross-stage fix handles a baby born in an earlier month than its postnatal visit (e.g. Birth in December, PNC visit in January): the answer either chooses boundaries that still see the earlier Birth-stage weight (e.g. ENROLLMENT with enrollment-date or PS_EVENTDATE:ZzYYXq4fJie cohort boundaries, or an EVENT PI on the Birth stage counted by birth date) or explicitly flags that EVENT_DATE boundaries on an ENROLLMENT PI would hide that birth and tests that case. An ENROLLMENT candidate with EVENT_DATE boundaries and no mention of the cross-month case fails

Explains the unchanged chart after yesterday's change as cached analytics responses, not as evidence the change didn't matter, and gives a concrete way to bypass the cache: POST /api/maintenance/cacheClear (or Data Administration > Maintenance > clear cache) or a neutral cache-busting query parameter (e.g. &_cb=<timestamp>). Does not require any specific cache duration (the DHIS2 default keyCacheStrategy is CACHE_1_MINUTE; SL demo databases set CACHE_TWO_WEEKS). A parameter that changes the result (e.g. skipRounding) is not a valid cache-buster
States that the Percent indicator type (factor 100) is not the cause and leaves it unchanged
Proposes a verification step specific to PIs: throwaway probe PIs, a line-level /api/analytics/events/query check, or boundary-date test events on both sides of a month edge

Programmatic: outputs/ contains a fixed metadata JSON file that parses, covers all three program indicators (the cross-stage PI may be replaced by new PIs, and the file must include the replacement), and every program indicator in it that uses event data has non-empty analyticsPeriodBoundaries and a count-type aggregation (not AVERAGE). An answer with no fixed metadata file fails
evals.notes: Debugging case with several independent silent PI bugs (AVERAGE on count, missing boundaries, cross-stage EVENT ref, cache) plus a false lead (indicator type) that must not be blamed.

evals.prompt: Before we copy the Sierra Leone demo's 'ANC 1-3 Dropout Rate' and 'ANC 3 Coverage' indicators into a new national 2.42 system, I want proof they compute what their names say. The SL demo instance is at http://dhis2-agent-sl242:8080 (admin/district). Can you check the definitions and test them properly, and give me a short report with the evidence?
evals.expected_output: Fetches both indicators and their types from the SL demo; validates numerators/denominators via GET /api/expressions/description and quotes the returned descriptions; lints referenced DEs (aggregationType, valueType, COCs in the current combo, zeroIsSignificant) and notes ANC 3 Coverage is annualized with an Expected pregnancies denominator; tests on a fresh EMPTY 2.42 instance (not the seeded demo) using the dataset dependency export plus indicators and indicatorTypes separately; enters distinct values per cell across two sibling org units with a zero-denominator case, checks imported+updated equals payload size, runs analytics and polls to completion, computes expected values two ways (engine and intent), checks parent = sum(num)/sum(den) and monthly vs yearly annualization; saves artifacts; reports agreement or the defect.
assertions: Validates each numerator and denominator with GET /api/expressions/description and reports the returned status/description for each
Checks the referenced data elements' configuration (aggregationType, valueType/domainType, and that any #{de.coc} COC belongs to the DE's current category combo), not only the expressions
Runs the data test on a fresh, empty instance (created without a seed, e.g. via the d2-broker) rather than by entering or reading data on the seeded SL demo
Imports the dataset dependency export and supplies the indicators and their indicator types separately, then confirms the indicator-type factors on the test instance
Enters distinct per-cell values (not constants) across at least two sibling org units under one parent, and checks the import with imported + updated == number of data values in the payload
Computes expected values two independent ways (re-evaluating the stored expression, and from the indicator's meaning) and compares both to analytics output
Checks the parent org unit value as sum of numerators over sum of denominators, and addresses the annualized flag on ANC 3 Coverage (monthly value scaled vs yearly)
Triggers analytics and waits for the ANALYTICS_TABLE task to complete before querying (or re-runs it after data changes)
evals.requires: dhis2-instance: Sierra Leone demo 2.42 (reference metadata) plus an empty unseeded 2.42 instance from the d2-broker (test)
evals.notes: Only live case: exercises the full testing.md method (description endpoints, lint, fresh-instance test, two-way expected values) and the trap of testing on the populated demo.
